title: Razorback traffic hedge for VPC rolling upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a Terraform-driven, traffic-hedging upgrade flow for private (VPC) data-plane runtime rollouts that guarantees zero-downtime and provides an immediate fast-path rollback. The feature combines preflight snapshotting, tenant-level heartbeat health gating, synthetic shadowing, and an incremental traffic hedge that shifts a conservative percentage of requests to the new runtime while continuously validating correctness and latency. The implementation spans: 1) Terraform/IaC hooks to create immutable upgrade artifacts and pre-upgrade snapshots; 2) a controller that manages staged traffic hedges based on per-tenant health signals; 3) KV priming and cache warming hooks exposed as REST probes; 4) a fast rollback path that re-routes hedge traffic away and rehydrates previous runtime if health thresholds trip. The ticket covers design, implementation, automated e2e tests, observability (dashboards + alerts), and an Ops runbook.
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting — aligned on objective: avoid tenant-visible errors and maintain p95 latency SLAs during upgrades. Decided to use 'hedge' terminology rather than 'canary' to emphasize symmetric routing and rollback guarantees.

2026-02-25: Design RFC posted to Confluence. Key trade-offs: synchronous shadowing vs sampled hedge; chose incremental hedge (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) to limit blast radius and provide production traffic validation for kernel scheduling changes.

2026-03-01: Prototype controller built that reads Terraform upgrade artifacts and applies staged routing via sidecar proxy rules. Initial synthetic probe failures revealed race in KV-priming step; added barrier and priming ack channel.
2026-03-05: Security review requested (KMS usage for snapshot metadata). Sec team requested explicit audit events for upgrade accept/rollback; added audit hooks to controller.

2026-03-09: e2e smoke tests run in staging using seeded tenant data. Observed 0.4% QPS variance and p95 latency within SLA. One transient error case during bulk-embedding requests — created ENG-707002 to investigate batching interactions.
2026-03-12: Ops runbook draft reviewed by SRE; added immediate rollback CLI and terraform plan preview step. Preparing for a phased rollout to customers on Dedicated and Private.
2026-03-13: Code PR opened for controller and TF module: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1209. Requesting review from Marco Liu (runtime) and Priya Shah (SRE).
notes: Controller will expose /priming-status and /healthcheck endpoints for orchestration
TF preflight hook will create immutable snapshot and record snapshot_id in upgrade artifact
Traffic hedge steps: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 80% -> 100%; health checks evaluated at each step
Health gating: tenant heartbeat (success ratio), p50/p95 latency regression checks, error-rate cap
Rollback fast-path: immediate 100% route revert + cache rehydration of previous runtime
Monitoring: alert on >0.5% uplift in error rate OR 20% p95 regression during a step
Follow-ups: ENG-707002 (batching interaction), PM-4120 (customer communication template)
